metaDescription: Four 80 pint dehumidifiers with a built-in or bundled condensate pump, compared on lift height, tank size and basement use, with a firm top pick.
expertTake: The AEOCKY with its 16.5 foot pump lift is the pick for most finished basements and utility rooms. The COSTWAY is the value choice if you want a big tank as a fallback. If your drain is at floor level and close, skip the pump entirely and buy a plain hose-drain unit.
introParagraphs: A condensate pump turns a dehumidifier from a bucket you must remember to empty into an appliance that disappears into a corner. The pump lifts water up and across to a sink, a laundry standpipe or a window, so the machine no longer depends on a floor drain below it.

That convenience adds a motor, a float switch and a length of tubing to the list of things that can clog or fail. Choosing well means knowing how high the pump lifts, how much water the machine holds when the pump is off, and who supplies the tubing.

products.name: AEOCKY 80 Pint Dehumidifier With Pump, up to 16.5 ft lift
products.description:
Lift height is the number that matters on a pump model, and AEOCKY advertises up to 16.5 feet. That is enough to clear a basement ceiling and reach a first-floor sink or a high window, which is the scenario where a pump earns its place. Most competitors in this group leave you guessing about the vertical reach.

The cabinet carries the Most Efficient 2025 designation, so the electricity used to chase 80 pints a day is lower than on an ordinary unit. The coverage claim of 4,500 sq ft is a little below the 5,000 to 5,500 sq ft claims of plain 80 pint models, which suggests a more realistic rating for a heavy-duty machine.

Expect to buy this one for the long haul. Check the pump discharge hose for kinks after installation and run a bucket of water through it each spring, because a pump that sits dry for months can stick. It costs more than the COSTWAY, and its price tier sits just below the CADPXS, so you are paying for lift height and the efficiency badge.
products.bestFor: Finished basements where the drain is above or far from the machine.

products.name: COSTWAY 80 Pint Dehumidifier With Pump, 2.2 gal tank
products.description:
COSTWAY lists three drain options in one cabinet: empty the detachable tank, run a gravity hose, or use the pump. That flexibility is the main selling point, because a power outage or a kinked pump line does not leave you with a flooded floor. A 2.2 gallon tank is also bigger than the tank on any plain 80 pint model in the neighboring guide.

The two-vent airflow design spreads dry air across the room rather than dumping it in one direction, and a 24-hour timer lets you run it only during the off-peak hours of your electric plan. The listing does not make an Energy Star Most Efficient claim, so judge it as a conventional compressor unit and expect a higher running cost than the AEOCKY.

It falls in the lower-middle price tier of this lineup, well below the AprilAire and CADPXS. For a finished basement where you want a pump but also a tank as a fallback, it is the sensible compromise. The tradeoff is less certainty about pump lift than the AEOCKY, so measure the vertical rise to your drain before buying.

products.name: CADPXS 80 Pint Commercial Crawl Space Dehumidifier With Pump
products.description:
Where the AEOCKY aims at a finished basement, CADPXS is built for the dark, cramped spaces under a house. The cabinet measures only 15.6 by 12 by 12.6 inches, small enough to slide through a crawl space access hatch and sit on a block pad. It pairs a pump with a drain hose so you can set it and leave.

A compact commercial box trades away comfort features. There is no Energy Star Most Efficient claim and no smart controls on this listing, so treat it as a workhorse that removes water and nothing more. Pump lift is not advertised, which is a real gap for a machine that may need to push water up and out a rim joist.

At the upper-middle price tier, it costs more than the COSTWAY and less than the AprilAire. Look at the crawl space itself before committing: a crawl space colder than about 60F shrinks every compressor unit's output, and a vapor barrier on the ground matters more than the machine. Treat this CADPXS as a tool for the stubborn part of the house.

products.name: AprilAire E080W 80 Pint Wi-Fi Dehumidifier With Pump

specList.label: Pump
specList.value: Low-profile condensate pump, bracket and tubing included

products.description:
AprilAire is the established name in whole-house humidity control, and the E080W is the only unit here sold as a bundle with a separate low-profile condensate pump, bracket and tubing. That arrangement keeps the pump outside the cabinet where you can service or swap it, instead of sealed inside the machine.

Wi-Fi and the AprilAire Connect app give remote setpoint control and alerts, which suits a home that sits empty part of the year. It carries Energy Star certification and shows up at the highest price tier of the lineup, so you pay noticeably more than for the COSTWAY or AEOCKY.

What you get for that money is a cleaner install and a brand with a service network, plus the ability to replace the pump alone if it fails. For a basement that serves the whole house, it is the premium route. If you only need a pump and a bucket fallback, the COSTWAY covers that for far less, so buy the AprilAire for the installation and support, not for extra pints.
products.bestFor: Whole-house humidity control where a serviceable external pump matters.
pros: External pump with bracket and tubing included
cons: Highest price tier in the group
Same 80 pint capacity as cheaper rivals

buyingCriteria.explanation: A condensate pump lifts water through a small tube, and its rated vertical lift drops as the tube gets longer. The AEOCKY advertises up to 16.5 feet, while the other three do not state a lift figure on their listings. Measure from the machine's outlet to the drain height, add the horizontal distance, and leave 20 percent margin. A pump that barely reaches will chatter and wear out.

buyingCriteria.criterion: What happens when the pump fails
buyingCriteria.explanation: Pumps clog, and floats stick after a dry winter. The COSTWAY includes a 2.2 gallon tank and a gravity hose alongside the pump, so a failure only means emptying a bucket. The CADPXS and AprilAire lean harder on the pump, so check the access to the pump housing before you commit. A machine you cannot reach with a screwdriver is a liability.

Eighty pints is a hot-room test number. Under the 65F and 60% RH condition used by the DOE since 2019, output reads about 40 percent lower. A pump model sized at 80 pints delivers closer to 50 to 56 pints in a cool damp basement, which is still plenty for roughly 2,500 to 4,000 sq ft of real use.

Crawl spaces and unheated basements often sit below 60F, where compressor coils frost and the machine cycles through defrost. Auto defrost prevents ice but does not restore capacity. For a space that stays cold, the AEOCKY or CADPXS commercial-style cabinets are better built than the home-oriented COSTWAY, but a true low-temperature unit would outperform all four.

Big dehumidifiers draw roughly 500 to 800 watts while running, and pump models are usually set up to run continuously. The AEOCKY Most Efficient 2025 designation matters here because a continuous machine accumulates thousands of hours. The AprilAire carries a regular Energy Star mark, and the COSTWAY and CADPXS make no efficiency claim on the listing.

Pump tubing is usually a thin vinyl line that must run without dips or kinks. Mount an external pump, like the AprilAire's, on its bracket at the right height so it can prime. Pumps click on and off, which is noticeable in a quiet room, so skip the bedroom-adjacent closet if you are sensitive to sound.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pump transparency
howWeEvaluated.description: Each listing was read for a stated lift height, a bundled pump or a built-in one. The AEOCKY advertises 16.5 feet; the AprilAire bundles a separate low-profile pump with bracket and tubing. A listing that says nothing about lift lost points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Failure fallback
howWeEvaluated.description: We asked what happens if the pump stops. COSTWAY offers a tank and a gravity hose alongside the pump, which gave it an edge. Units that depend only on the pump were ranked by how accessible that pump appears to be.

howWeEvaluated.title: Efficiency claims
howWeEvaluated.description: Working from listing data, units claiming Energy Star or Most Efficient status ranked higher for continuous-duty use, but only where the listing named the tier. Efficiency matters more on a pump model because it is expected to run for long stretches.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: Repeated owner comments were weighed, including pump noise, clogged lines after a winter shutdown and how the humidistat tracks a separate meter. We discounted single complaints and looked for patterns across the listings.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup balance
howWeEvaluated.description: The four picks were separated by role: finished basement, value, crawl space and whole-house. AprilAire sits at the top price tier and COSTWAY at the lower-middle, so we weighed what each premium buys against the 80 pint capacity they all share.

cards.label: Built-in pump
cards.text: The AEOCKY, COSTWAY and CADPXS keep the pump inside the cabinet, so there is one power cord and nothing to mount. The cost is service: if the pump fails, you often send in or replace the whole unit. A tank fallback, as on the COSTWAY, softens that risk.

cards.label: External pump
cards.text: The AprilAire bundle uses a low-profile pump on its own bracket. You can swap a failed pump without touching the dehumidifier, and place it where the tubing runs cleanly. It needs a second outlet and a mounting spot near the machine.

howToChoose.note: Pick a built-in pump for simplicity and an external pump if you value serviceability.

howToChoose.subheading: For Utility Rooms and Laundry Areas Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A short, kink-free tube run to a laundry standpipe or utility sink, a stated lift height and a cabinet that can sit on a stand. Laundry rooms add steam and lint, so a washable filter matters.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The AEOCKY is the best fit because its advertised 16.5 ft lift clears a standpipe easily. The COSTWAY is the budget alternative when you also want a tank to fall back on during a power outage.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The machine will run continuously or drain upward more than 10 feet. The AEOCKY's lift rating and efficiency tier justify the upper price tier, and the AprilAire is worth it if serviceability and an app are priorities.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your drain is near and below the machine, or you only need a pump a few months a year. The COSTWAY gives you the pump and a spare tank at the lower-middle tier, and a plain hose-drain 80 pint unit may be cheaper still.

maintenance.why: A pump left dry over winter can stick or clog with sediment. Pour a bucket of clean water through the tank and watch it discharge.
Any dip in the line holds water and drops lift height. Re-seat the tube and secure it with clips so it slopes steadily to the drain.
A dirty mesh chokes airflow and lets the coil frost. Rinse and dry before refitting.
Dust on the fins reduces heat transfer and lengthens run cycles. Unplug first and use a soft brush.
A stuck float either stops the machine early or lets water overflow. Lift it by hand and confirm the unit shuts off and restarts.

faq.q: Is a pump worth it on an 80 pint unit?
faq.a: Only if gravity cannot reach your drain. A hose to a floor drain is simpler and has one less part to fail. A pump suits a laundry standpipe, a sink above the machine or a window outlet.

faq.q: How far can these pumps push water?
faq.a: Only the AEOCKY advertises a figure, up to 16.5 feet. Lift drops as the tube lengthens, so a long horizontal run reduces the usable height. Ask the seller for the pump curve if your rise exceeds about 10 feet.

faq.q: Why does the pump unit cost more than a plain one?
faq.a: The pump motor, float and tubing add parts and testing. The AprilAire bundle is the highest tier because the pump is a separate serviceable component, while the COSTWAY keeps the premium low by building the pump in.
Yes, a short click and buzz each time the reservoir empties. It is rarely loud but noticeable in a quiet room, so place the machine away from a bedroom wall.

faq.q: Can I run it in a cold crawl space?
faq.a: You can, but output falls as the coil cools, and below roughly 60F the unit spends time defrosting. A vapor barrier on the ground and sealed vents usually help more than a larger machine.

faq.q: How do I winterize the pump?
faq.a: Drain the tank, run the pump until it clears, and disconnect the tubing so water does not freeze in the line. Store the unit upright in a space above freezing.
